Our Developer plan is a great choice for personal projects. You will have 1 free seat with access to LangSmith (5k base traces/month included). The Plus plan is for teams that want to self-serve with moderate usage and collaboration needs. You can purchase unlimited seats with access to LangSmith (10k base traces/month included). You will be able to ship agents with our managed LangSmith Deployment service, with 1 free dev-sized deployment included. The Enterprise plan is for teams that need more advanced administration, security, support, or deployment options. Contact our sales team to learn more. Do you offer a plan for startups? Yes! We offer a Startup Plan for LangSmith, designed for early-stage companies building agentic applications. You’ll get discounted rates and generous free trace allotments to build with confidence from day one. ‍ Apply here to get started with startup pricing. When will I be billed? For the Developer or Plus Plan, seats are billed monthly on the 1st or pro-rated if added mid-month (no credit for removed seats); traces are billed monthly in arrears for your usage. Enterprise plans are invoiced annually upfront. Will you train on the data that I send to LangSmith? No. LangSmith does not use your data to train models. Your traces, prompts, and outputs remain private to your organization. See LangSmith Terms of Service for more information. What is a seat? A seat is a distinct user inside your organization. We consider the total number of users (including invited users) to determine the number of seats to bill. I have a developer account, can I upgrade my account to the plus or enterprise plan? Yes, Developer plan users can easily upgrade to the Plus plan on the Plans and Billing page. For the Enterprise plan, please contact our sales team to discuss your needs. LangSmith Observability & Evaluation Questions What is a trace? Can it contain multiple events? A trace represents a single execution of your application—whether it’s an agent, evaluator, or playground session. It can include many individual steps, such as LLM calls and other tracked events. Here's an example of a single trace. What is the difference between a base trace and an extended trace? Base traces have a shorter retention period of 14 days and cost $2.50 per 1k traces. Extended traces have a longer retention period of 400 days and cost $5.00 per 1k traces. You can "upgrade" base traces to extended traces at $2.50 per 1k traces. Why would I upgrade a base trace to an extended trace? Base traces are short-lived (14-day retention) and ideal for quick debugging or ad-hoc analysis. They’re priced for volume and short-term utility. Extended traces, on the other hand, are retained for 400 days and often include valuable feedback—whether from users, evaluators, or human labelers. This feedback makes them essential for ongoing improvement and model tuning (higher utility), which comes with a higher price point. LangSmith lets you choose the right retention for each trace, helping you balance cost and value. LangSmith Deployment Questions Does LangSmith Deployment include any free deployments? Plus plans include 1 free dev-sized deployment. If you spin up additional dev-sized or production-sized deployments, you’ll be charged by usage (deployment runs and uptime). For my free Dev agent deployment for LangSmith Deployment, is there a cap on the number of deployment runs? If you’re on the Plus plan, you get 1 free dev-sized agent deployment – all usage in this deployment will be free no matter how many deployment runs you execute. How do you define deployment runs? A deployment run is one end-to-end invocation of a LangGraph agent deployed via LangSmith Deployment. Nodes and subgraphs within a single agent execution are not charged separately. Calls to other LangGraph agents (through RemoteGraph or the LangGraph SDK or the API directly) are charged separately, to the deployment that hosts the agent being called. An interrupt for human-in-the-loop creates a separate deployment run when resuming. For Plus plans, Deployment Runs are billed at $0.005 each. Enterprise pricing is customized based on customer requirements, including support needs. What does uptime mean for LangSmith Deployment usage? Uptime is the duration your deployment’s database is live and persisting state. Uptime will be tracked as soon as your deployment is live and ends when you shut it down. Dev agent deployments are typically short-lived (used during iteration, then deleted) – whereas Production agent deployments stay live and are updated via revisions (rather than being deleted). When should I use a dev-sized deployment vs. a production-sized agent deployment? We recommend using the production-sized deployment for any customer-facing agent. Dev-sized agent deployments are intended for testing and do not support horizontal scaling, backups, or performance optimizations needed in production. LangSmith Fleet Questions What is a Fleet run? A Fleet run is a single execution (a complete invocation) of an agent. Runs occur when you create, test, or run an agent. A Fleet run includes any message delivered to the agent through configured triggers (including third-party integrations or other connected services) as well as messages sent directly through the Fleet user interface (e.g., via the chat interface). An interrupt for human-in-the-loop creates a separate Fleet run when resuming. An execution failure does not count as a Fleet run. Are model costs included with Fleet pricing? No. Model usage is billed separately by your model provider. Fleet lets you choose the model you want (for example, Anthropic, OpenAI, Gemini, or another provider) and connect it using your provider API key. More information on configuring models in our docs . Are agent tools included with Fleet pricing? Fleet includes built-in tools and supports connecting third-party tools via a remote MCP server. Third-party tools typically require you to authenticate with your account, and any fees or usage charges are billed by the third-party provider. More information on setting up tool keys in our docs . Are Fleet runs automatically traced in LangSmith, and do they count toward billing? Yes. Every Fleet run is automatically traced in LangSmith. These traces are attributed to the user’s account and count toward usage-based billing under the customer’s LangSmith plan. Can I self-host Fleet? Self-hosting for Fleet is currently available in Beta. Contact our sales team to learn more. How do I disable Fleet? Yaser Alkayale, Co-founder / CivCore Frequently asked questions How is Ravion different from Terraform Cloud or Spacelift? Ravion does everything you'd expect from a Terraform automation platform: remote plans and applies, managed state, versioned resource history, drift detection, approval gates, and policy checks. The difference is that modules are the product. Each module also carries its builds, deploys, rollbacks, logs, and metrics, so developers get a self-service interface instead of a pile of HCL and a run queue. Learn about stacks How is Ravion different from a PaaS? A PaaS hosts your app on their infrastructure, and you're capped by whatever they choose to expose. Ravion provisions everything in your own AWS account, so you get dedicated infrastructure, direct cloud pricing, easier compliance, and no wall to hit as you scale. The developer experience feels like a PaaS. The ceiling is the entire cloud, and there's no painful migration waiting for you later. Read our product philosophy Do I have to write Terraform? No. Most teams start with our standard library of production-ready modules, including VPCs, ECS and EC2 services, RDS, Aurora, ElastiCache, Lambda, and static sites, configured through typed inputs in the dashboard or a YAML file. When you need something custom, bring your own Terraform: run it through Ravion directly, or package it into a reusable module with typed inputs your team can self-serve. Explore the standard library Can I use CloudFormation, Pulumi, or CDK? Not today. Runners are temporary EC2 instances in your own account, and the native modules cover the common AWS building blocks. A trace represents a single execution of your application—whether it’s an agent, evaluator, or playground session. It can include many individual steps, such as LLM calls and other tracked events. Here's an example of a single trace. What is the difference between a base trace and an extended trace? Base traces have a shorter retention period of 14 days and cost $2.50 per 1k traces. Extended traces have a longer retention period of 400 days and cost $5.00 per 1k traces. You can "upgrade" base traces to extended traces at $2.50 per 1k traces. Why would I upgrade a base trace to an extended trace? Base traces are short-lived (14-day retention) and ideal for quick debugging or ad-hoc analysis. They’re priced for volume and short-term utility. Extended traces, on the other hand, are retained for 400 days and often include valuable feedback—whether from users, evaluators, or human labelers. This feedback makes them essential for ongoing improvement and model tuning (higher utility), which comes with a higher price point. LangSmith lets you choose the right retention for each trace, helping you balance cost and value. LangSmith Deployment Questions Does LangSmith Deployment include any free deployments? A deployment run is one end-to-end invocation of a LangGraph agent deployed via LangSmith Deployment. Nodes and subgraphs within a single agent execution are not charged separately. Calls to other LangGraph agents (through RemoteGraph or the LangGraph SDK or the API directly) are charged separately, to the deployment that hosts the agent being called. Uptime is the duration your deployment’s database is live and persisting state. Uptime will be tracked as soon as your deployment is live and ends when you shut it down. A Fleet run is a single execution (a complete invocation) of an agent. Runs occur when you create, test, or run an agent. A Fleet run includes any message delivered to the agent through configured triggers (including third-party integrations or other connected services) as well as messages sent directly through the Fleet user interface (e.g., via the chat interface). Fleet lets you choose the model you want (for example, Anthropic, OpenAI, Gemini, or another provider) and connect it using your provider API key. More information on configuring models in our docs . Third-party tools typically require you to authenticate with your account, and any fees or usage charges are billed by the third-party provider. More information on setting up tool keys in our docs . Are Fleet runs automatically traced in LangSmith, and do they count toward billing? Yes. Every Fleet run is automatically traced in LangSmith. Engine is metered in LCUs (LangChain Compute Units), which are consumed during each Engine run. 1 LCU costs $1.50. What does a LangChain Compute Unit (LCU) represent? An LCU represents a unit of work done by Engine. This includes the compute, infrastructure, and underlying model usage needed to analyze traces, identify issues, and propose fixes to your agent. How are LCUs calculated? Typical usage depends on whether Engine is running for the first time or on its regular schedule: Initial run: about 30 to 40 LCUs Recurring runs: about 10 to 15 LCUs every 6 hours These ranges are estimates. Actual usage depends on the amount of work Engine performs, including the volume of traces analyzed, the number of issues surfaced, the number of proposed fixes generated, and the complexity of your application. How often does Engine run? Engine is scheduled to run once every 6 hours. Is model usage included in the cost? Yes. Engine pricing includes the underlying model usage required for analysis and fix generation. Where can I see my LCU usage? You can view your organization’s LCU usage in your LangSmith billing console by visiting Settings > Billing. Learn more . Are LCUs included in my plan? Plus plans: LCUs are an additional charge on top of your monthly license fee and any other product usage. Enterprise plans: LCUs are charged against your committed LangChain credits. How do I disable Engine? Ask your Organization Admin to turn off Engine in the Settings page by following instructions here . Once Engine is disabled, it will stop running on its regular schedule and will no longer consume LCUs. LangSmith Sandboxes Questions How is Sandbox uptime calculated? Sandboxes are designed as ephemeral compute environments and are billed per second. LangSmith Sandboxes have configurable TTLs so inactive sandboxes shut down automatically. Frequently Asked Questions Below are the more common questions we get asked. To learn more, book a demo with our team. Is Directus free to self-host? A commercial license is only required for production projects within entities exceeding $5 million in total annual finances. Inspired by Unity’s software license , we’ve defined total finances as the largest of your aggregate gross revenues, entire budget, and/or funding (no matter the source) — each calculated based on the most recent 12-month period. If your total finances are under $5,000,000 USD, you are free to use Directus however you see fit. If you’re using Directus in a non-production instance, this change doesn’t affect you. If your total finances are over $5,000,000 and you’re using Directus in production, you will have to purchase a commercial license. To illustrate the various use cases: Individual developer making a non-commercial hobby project — No cost Small business with total finances under $5,000,000 — No cost Large enterprise non-production use — No cost Large enterprise production use — Commercial license required Small agency building projects for others — Depends on your client Please refer to our software license for a detailed description of terms, or contact our team with any questions. How do I purchase a commercial license? Purchasing a license is super easy – grab some time to chat with our licensing team to discuss your needs and use case. Why BSL 1.1? BSL is a simpler way of licensing software compared to traditional methods. The source code is openly accessible, and non-commercial use is free. The code will automatically become open-source within three years, under a GPL-compatible license. There are many software licenses available for a wide variety of (specialty) use cases. We felt that BSL1.1 came the closest to keeping the spirit of Open Source intact while allowing us to make sure it’s financially sustainable. We also noticed that many of our favorite projects, like Sentry, CockroachDB, and Couchbase all have successfully adopted BSL as their license. Can you provide my company with a demo? For a full demo of our Enterprise cloud offering and features, book some time with our enterprise team . What is the difference between "Studio Users" and regular "Users"? Studio Users are users that have access to the Directus Data Studio. These are typically members of your team who use the studio to interact with your data – like creating new blog posts, editing page content, managing assets, or more. The technical criteria for a Studio User is: At least one policy with 'Admin Access' enabled. At least one policy with 'App Access' enabled, allowing access to the Data Studio. Other users that ONLY access Directus via the APIs do not count towards your Studio User total. An API Only user might be a person who's interacting with your frontend application, an internal microservice that fetches or pushes data to Directus, or a third party system sending data to Directus. Where can I see my invoices? You can access all of your team's invoices and transaction history directly through our Cloud Dashboard . Do you offer support for self-hosted projects? Anyone can access our Community Support and knowledge base on GitHub Discussion . Premium support options are only available to Enterprise Cloud customers or paid agreements. Contact our team to discuss further. How much do Enterprise Cloud projects cost? Enterprise pricing is tailored to each project's specific requirements. Please contact our team to coordinate a customized proposal. Do you offer non-profit or open-source discounts? Yes, we do! Being open source ourselves, we're aware of how important it is to support open-source maintainers. If you are the maintainer of an open-source project (see policy below), contact us to discuss available discounts. Firecrawl is free for the first 500 pages (500 free credits). After that, you can upgrade to our Hobby, Standard or Growth plans for more credits and higher rate limits. AI agents can get started using the onboarding skill at https://www.firecrawl.dev/agent-onboarding/SKILL.md which handles signup and API key creation in one smooth flow. Is there a pay-per-use plan instead of monthly? We currently do not offer a pay-per-use plan, instead you can upgrade to our Hobby, Standard or Growth plans for more credits and higher rate limits. Do credits roll over to the next month? In short, no — credits do not roll over to the next month/year. Credit packs follow their own billing period. Search costs 1 credit per result. Scrape costs 1 credit per page. Interact costs 5 credits per action. There are advanced features available which cost additional credits. Search costs 1 credit per result. Scrape costs 1 credit per page. Interact costs 5 credits per action. There are advanced features available which cost additional credits. Please contact us . How does Terragrunt Pipelines handle plan output when deploying infrastructure stacks? When deploying a stack of infrastructure units, Terragrunt Pipelines will concurrently generate a plan for all the infrastructure units in the stack, and display them in a single pull request / merge request comment as separate plans. What happens if multiple PR/MRs interact with the same resources? Terragrunt Pipelines uses an "apply after merge" approach. This means that while multiple PRs are proposing changes to the same resources, there’s only ever a single source of truth for the infrastructure that will be provisioned (the Infrastructure as Code on the deploy branch e.g. main). During initial implementation we guide teams to using features of their SCM platform to enforce branch protection rules that ensure that plans are recent and applies are predictable. Is Uploadcare a fit? Absolutely! We’ll price-match your current contracts with CDN and other vendors, and migrate you for free! Get in touch with our sales team to learn more. How long will it take to integrate Uploadcare with my web or mobile app? It usually takes anywhere from 5 mins to a few days, depending on your use case. We offer ready-made libraries for all popular frameworks and follow the API-first approach. Plus, everyone on the Uploadcare customer support team is an engineer, so they can actually help you to build something cool! What CDN do you use? Uploadcare works with multiple CDNs including Cloudfront, Akamai and Fastly. Get in touch if you want to migrate your current contract or use another CDN. Can I put a CDN or caching layer on top of Uploadcare? Yes, but only with a custom plan. Get in touch with our team to discuss the details. What types of files does Uploadcare support? Uploadcare supports any file types: images, videos or documents, up to 5TB each. Can my users upload files from Google Drive, Dropbox, Box and other cloud storage services? Uploadcare has built-in integrations with more than ten cloud storage services and social media platforms including Facebook and etc. Your users can choose files from anywhere to upload to your platform. And, if you work with sensitive content, you can set up your own apps so your users will feel safer when they provide access to their files. What are Operations? Operations are various actions associated with your files and API usage. Actions like uploading a file, making requests, or requesting transformations on your images are considered operations. Different actions have different operation costs, If you’re curious about more information on how operations are calculated you can read this article . What counts as Traffic? In Uploadcare, “Traffic” refers to the data transferred both from Uploadcare CDN to your end-users and between Uploadcare CDN and Uploadcare’s servers. Uploadcare offers image and video optimization tools, which are quite handy because they help you significantly reduce your traffic usage. By optimizing your files, you’re essentially reducing the file size without noticeably affecting the quality, meaning less data needs to be transferred, hence, less traffic used. What counts as Storage? When it comes to Storage in Uploadcare, it’s all about the total size of the original files stored in your account. This includes every single image, video, document, or other type of file that you’ve uploaded to Uploadcare. Unlike in some other systems, only the original versions of your files count towards your storage — not any transformations or alterations you might have made. It’s important to note that this metric is cumulative, meaning it adds up over time. The storage counter doesn’t reset at the start of a new billing cycle. Can I use Uploadcare for free? Yes, we offer a Free plan designed for small-scale projects. It is designed to allow users to explore and experience the features and capabilities of Uploadcare without any cost. However, it’s important to note that the Free plan may have certain limitations compared to our paid subscription plans. If you require additional information about the specific features and limitations of the Free plan, feel free to contact Uploadcare’s sales team . What happens if my Free plan limit is reached? The Free plan is designed for very small-scale projects—perfect for hobby use, prototyping, or testing an MVP. However, exceeding its usage limits will result in a temporary suspension until the start of the next month. To avoid any interruptions, we recommend upgrading to one of our paid plans—which offer more generous limits and ensure uninterrupted access to all features. How do you charge me? When will I get billed? We charge for our services through a subscription model. There are two types of fees: Subscription Fees and Usage Fees. The Subscription Fee is paid upfront when you sign up and covers a certain amount of usage for the chosen monthly or annual period. If you exceed the allowed usage limits in your subscription plan, we will charge Usage Fees at the end of each month. For more detailed information on the terms and conditions, including the Order Form, taxes, and refund policies, please refer to the full terms of service provided by Uploadcare. What happens if I exceed my plan limits? Uploadcare limits are soft, and if you go above them, overage fees will apply automatically. Please contact us to discuss a plan which aligns best with your needs. Which payment methods do you support? Uploadcare currently accepts major credit and debit cards for payment. In addition, if you’re subscribed to the Enterprise plan, you also have the option to make payments via bank transfers. Please note, alternatives like PayPal, Bitcoin, and similar methods are not currently supported. If you need further information or assistance with payment methods, feel free to get in touch with Uploadcare’s sales team . Who has ownership of the files and data uploaded to Uploadcare? Uploadcare values your ownership rights and privacy. All files and data you upload to Uploadcare remain your property. You maintain ownership of your files and data, and Uploadcare merely acts as a service provider to store and handle your files based on your instructions. Can Uploadcare store sensitive files and data? Yes, Uploadcare is SOC2 and HIPAA-compliant, ensuring that industry-standard security measures are in place to protect your files and data. As a trusted file management service, Uploadcare prioritizes the security and integrity of your information. Uploadcare provides a 99.9% Service Level Agreement (SLA) on all paid plans, ensuring high availability and reliability of the services. Additionally, Uploadcare systems maintain over 99.99% monthly uptime figures for most regions. For more specific details about Uploadcare’s security certifications, compliance standards, and the SLA, check out the Trust Center . How is the cost of adaptive bitrate streaming calculated? The cost is based on the number of resolution options and the duration of the video. Each resolution is billed separately. Each 10 seconds of video requires 20 operations. The duration is rounded up to the nearest 10 seconds. For example, a 52-second video with three resolutions (360p, 720p, 1080p) requires: (6 × 20 operations) × 3 resolutions = 360 operations What resolution options are available for videos? There are three resolution options: 360p, 720p, and 1080p. The resolution is based on the smaller side of the video. Videos are never upscaled; if the original video is 900p, the highest resolution will remain 900p. If the original video is smaller than 720p or 1080p, those resolutions will not be created. What happens if my video’s duration doesn’t align with 10-second intervals? Video durations are rounded up to the nearest 10-second increment. For instance: A 52-second video is rounded up to 60 seconds. Billing is then calculated based on this rounded duration. Are all resolution options always generated? No, the resolution options depend on the original video’s quality: If the original video is smaller than a resolution option (e.g., 720p or 1080p), those resolutions are not generated. This ensures no unnecessary upscaling in processing. Start building for free Get started Questions? Self-Hosted Agents: Automatically get 5 extra concurrent runs per agent, allowing you to easily manage and scale to concurrency. Why doesn't Scalr use concurrency-based pricing? Concurrency-based pricing — the model used by some alternatives — sells a fixed number of parallel run slots. The structural problem is that there is no setting that's right: too few slots and engineers queue during releases and incidents, too many and the customer is paying for idle capacity. The model also fails hardest exactly when throughput matters most, throttling parallel fixes during incident response while additional slots require procurement under pressure. Capacity planning becomes the customer's problem (forecasting peaks, monitoring utilization, engaging procurement to purchase additional slots as needs increase). Usage-based, per-run pricing avoids these failure modes by charging only for runs that actually executed — one more run costs one more run, and there is no slot to over- or under-provision. That is why Scalr bills per run instead of per concurrent slot. Who is Scalr for? Scalr is for platform engineers who want to build and manage their platform at scale while enabling developer self-service. How much does it cost? Business is usage-based at $0.99 per run with volume discounts (for example, 100 runs is $99 per month), and it starts at 5 concurrent runs that can be increased for free. Everything else is identical on both plans: unlimited users, unlimited environments, role-based access control with custom roles at the account, environment, or workspace scope, SAML 2.0 single sign-on (Okta, Microsoft Entra, JumpCloud, Google Workspace, and any other SAML 2.0 provider) at no extra charge, and the full set of core features such as drift detection, policy enforcement, and the module and provider registries. How does Scalr differentiate? Scalr is a cost effective, drop-in replacement for Terraform Cloud, with feature parity and better GitOps support. Install the lightweight agent on your Linux server with a single command, and metrics start appearing in your dashboard within 60 seconds. No configuration files to edit, no dependencies to install. What Linux distributions does Fivenines support? Fivenines supports Ubuntu, Debian, Rocky Linux, AlmaLinux, Arch Linux, CloudLinux, CentOS, and most other mainstream Linux distributions. Cypress App is an open-source, downloadable application that runs your tests in a browser. It is free to use and is provided under the MIT License. Cypress Cloud is a SaaS web app that pairs with our open-source app, making it easy to scale your test runs and debug failed tests. Transform how you test in CI, and push your code with confidence, every time. What counts as a test result? Cypress Cloud considers each run of individual it() functions as a test result. Only test results which are recorded to Cloud (with the --record flag) are counted. Local runs while in development are not counted. Skipped tests, or anything else that prevents a test from running will not be counted. Our experienced Technical Solutions Consultant specialize in Cypress, serving as trusted advisors to optimize your testing strategies. They offer tailored best practice sessions, analyzing workflows, and suggesting industry-proven improvements for enhanced efficiency. Your TSC provides dedicated technical support, ensuring swift issue resolution and keeping you updated on product developments. Every time a cy.prompt command runs, in open mode, or run mode, that counts as a single cy.prompt execution. Usage is treated consistently whether authoring and running tests locally, or in CI runs.
